chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: The Village Vanguard: the Three Flames, folk acts and bop
summary: She worked there with groups, folk-oriented bills including Leadbelly, Pete Seeger, the Weavers and Judy Holliday.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: At the Village Vanguard did you have a regular accompanist there?

Yeah, at one time I worked with the Three Flames which were a very good group. They were a comedy group, Roy Testamark, Carl Lynch, on guitar and Oh, Roy Haines—Tiger Haines. And I sang and they accompanied me. And another piano player by the name of Clarence Williams. He has his own trio there. And I'm trying to think of some of the guys. As I said before
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

the first group that I sang with at the Village Vanguard was a group made up of, it had Ralph Sutton on piano and Max Kaminsky on trumpet. It was Max Kaminsky's group. I think he had four pieces, the piano, trumpet, bass and drum. But off and on at the Vanguard I worked with trios and they had acts on the bill like Pete Seeger, Professor Irwin Corey. They had a magician on there who did an act with a puppet on his hand, Jerry Marshall I believe his name was. And what's his name, the comedian, Wally Cox.

And at one time Leadbelly was on the bill. In fact Pete Seeger was the act and I went to work one night and I saw this man standing out in front of the Village Vanguard and I didn't know who it was. And so I struck up a conversation with him and I thought it was just a customer who would come in later. So I had a little dressing room and I went in there and changed my clothes and when I came out I heard this singing and it was Leadbelly, the same person I was talking to out in the front. But I got a chance to work with a lot of different acts down there. The Village Vanguard
had people like Judy Holliday and the Weavers,/The Reviewers, or something like that. In fact the Village Vanguard is very noted for being a showcase for alot of different type acts.
Well not it has been a little bit more exclusively jazz.
Yeah, well since Mel Louis and Thad Jones went in there with the big band they kept it open for awhile. And now they have mostly just music.
That sounds very much like a folk oriented line-up that you're describing.
